evidence.title: U.S. Looks to Iceland as It Expands Military Footprint in Arctic

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. military Arctic resource-allocation and deployment records
occurrences.quote_span: The U.S. push to devote more military resources to the Arctic is colliding with competing demands elsewhere.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. State Department itinerary for Marco Rubio's October 2026 NATO allies tour
occurrences.quote_span: Rubio’s visit—part of a three-day tour of North Atlantic Treaty Organization allies that includes Greece and Portugal—comes as the U.S. turns military attention back on the Arctic after Washington largely deprioritized the region after the Cold War.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. Navy and Keflavik Air Base visitor and aircraft deployment records
occurrences.quote_span: On Tuesday, Rubio toured a U.S. Navy P-8A Poseidon at Keflavik Air Base, one of the maritime patrol aircraft that rotate through Iceland to hunt and track submarines across the North Atlantic.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.checkable_against: Transcript or recording of Marco Rubio's October 6, 2026 remarks
occurrences.quote_span: “There’s interest in doing more together,” Rubio said, praising Iceland for allowing “the U.S. military to project power using your land, your air, your sea, giving us a critical outpost for monitoring clandestine behavior and deterring our adversaries.”
occurrences.speaker: Marco Rubio
occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.checkable_against: Transcript or recording of Marco Rubio's October 6, 2026 remarks
occurrences.quote_span: “The reality of it is the world has changed over the last 20 years,” Rubio said. “Our focus has changed. There’s a lot of focus on the Arctic.”

occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. State Department readout and Icelandic government records of Rubio's meetings
occurrences.quote_span: In meetings with Icelandic officials, Rubio said the administration was open to expanding security cooperation, citing Iceland’s infrastructure, technology and surveillance capabilities.
occurrences.speaker: Marco Rubio
occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.checkable_against: U.S. State Department records of Marco Rubio's October 6, 2026 visit to Iceland
occurrences.quote_span: REYKJAVIK—Secretary of State Marco Rubio brought President Trump’s Arctic ambitions to Iceland on Tuesday, looking to build on a deal that emerged from Trump’s push to take control of Greenland as the U.S. expands its military reach across the region.

occurrences.subject: Marco Rubio's visit to Iceland and U.S.-Iceland security cooperation

occurrences.quote_span: While last month’s deal fell short of Trump’s demands to control Greenland, a self-governing territory that is part of Denmark, it paved the way for a larger U.S. military presence.
